newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gold trade sees Dubai imports overtaking '96 levels.
newsitem.headline: Gold trade sees Dubai imports overtaking '96 levels.

text.p: Dubai bullion imports so far this year have surged to the record levels of 1996 in a gold rush encouraged by weak world prices and rising demand from the Indian subcontinent, traders and officials said on Sunday.
They estimated that by the end of July, imports to the Gulf Arab emirate had reached 350 tonnes, about the same quantity imported throughout 1996.
"Prices have dropped this year and we have had good demand. This year Dubai is going to hit a record as far as imports are concerned," one trader told Reuters.
"By the end of July, gold imports reached about the same amount as in all of 1996," he said.

An official at the World Gold Council (WGC), owned by major gold producers and which promotes gold usage, said import figures for the month of July were not available yet, but agreed the trend appeared to confirm the traders' estimates.
"Imports are surging because demand has been extremely high from major consuming markets, including India," said D.V. Pathy, WGC manager for Gulf countries.
"The price of gold is extremely low and that is also a reason, because people find an opportunity to invest in gold."

Traders have said they expect Dubai gold imports to reach up to 500 tonnes in 1997. WGC figures show that 307.75 tonnes were imported in the first half of 1997, compared to 169.27 during the same period last year.
Dubai is the main source of gold imported to India. Around three quarters of Dubai's gold imports are re-exported to India, the world's second most populous nation after China.
Dubai exported about 35 tonnes to Pakistan last year and traders expect to ship some 60 tonnes this year.

Gold prices have fallen sharply since February under threat of selling from central banks as they reviewed the worth of holding gold reserves. Prices have dropped from around $368 at the beginning of the year to around $325 now.
Reserves held by central banks and other institutions total around 35,000 tonnes.
International spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $326.20/$326.70 an ounce, above the $324.50/325.00 quoted a week earlier, but lower than the $328.60/$329.10 seen on July 20.
Traders in Dubai said demand for gold remained high despite the sharp price fluctuations as investors braced for a rise in the value of the precious metal.
They said the end of India's monsoon rains around mid-September, coupled with the start then of the wedding season, was also expected to boost demand.
In January, India liberalised gold trade regulations, allowing non resident Indians to bring 10 kg (22 lb) of gold into the country every six months -- double the previous limit.
"Prices have gone down and there is already very good demand from India," another trader told Reuters, estimating demand this week was 25 percent more than it had been the previous week.
Another trader said he had seen little change in buying interest in the past week, but predicted business would pick up as the monsoon season came to an end.
Dubai's benchmark TT bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted on Sunday at between 4,505 and 4,515 dirhams ($1,227-$1,230) from 4,491 dirhams the previous week.
($1 = 3.67 dirhams)
